scenarios.title: Soiled face turned away from the spray source
scenarios.test: A dessert plate with oven-dried egg yolk on its eating face standing upright in the wide gap of the rear rows of the lower basket: face to the arm axis (A) against turned round in the same place (B). Beside it, the plate as the loading physics seats it in R1 slot 5: facing the axis (C), and put in reversed and left to settle (D)
scenarios.adapted: A porcelain dessert plate stands in for the dinner plate. A and B are set poses: the plate stands exactly upright (no lean) about 56 mm right of the arm axis, where the tines lean apart and leave room for it either way round; the runner checks that it cuts into nothing. In a slot between tines the same plate cannot simply be turned round: the tines lean outwards, the seated plate (C) faces the axis tipped 10 degrees up, and a reversed plate (D) falls back against the tines and lies 34 degrees from the vertical with its face to the wall and down. C and D are reported as supporting evidence.
scenarios.stages: water: jets (line of sight), droplets, run-off; soil: removal laws; load: physics (how a reversed plate sits)

expected.stated: f_jet on the soiled face drops to about 0
expected.tolerance: negative control: at most twice the stated limit, either sign

expected.stated: for oven-dried protein and starch, -1 to -2
expected.tolerance: stated range, a factor of two or one score point either way; the sign must be right

checks.quantity: share of the egg yolk left on the face, B - A

expected.stated: removal depends on how often the spot is hit
expected.tolerance: direction only: the checklist gives no size; under 0.01 counts as no effect

checks.quantity: fraction of time the soiled face is under a direct jet, settled reversed plate (D) over the seated one (C)

expected.stated: f_jet on the soiled face drops to about 0

scenarios.title: Plate pitch too small
scenarios.test: Rows of IEC dinner plates with egg yolk in the rear lane of the lower basket: two to a slot (about 7 mm between the pair, B), one per slot (18.25 mm, A), every second slot (36.5 mm, C); the plate at slot 6 is scored on its upper half (in B the one of the pair whose face is covered by the other)
scenarios.adapted: The tines of the Bosch fix the pitch at 18.25 mm, so the checklist's 12, 20 and 30 mm become two plates to a slot, every slot and every second slot. Seven plates per row (eight when crowded). All rows are settled by the loading physics; the crowded row has pairs in slots 2, 4, 6 and 8, so the covered plate of a pair has its face about 7 mm behind its partner while the partner faces an open slot.
